purpose: Record an independent visual source-image review of the official Turkana North Form 34B final TOTAL row and preserve an unexplained internal source denominator conflict without promotion.

sample.review_context_note: Rendered at 300 DPI (3-page official IEBC Form 34B PDF; page 2 of 3 is the polling-station table page whose final row is labelled TOTAL). Every page of the form (1 and 2) was reviewed for a special-facility polling station (prison, hospital, etc.) that might explain the registered-voters gap against the governed denominator; none was found.

review.reviewed_by: Claude Sonnet 5 (Anthropic), acting as an independent Kenya Data Atlas contributor agent
review.independence_note: The official Form 34B PDF was downloaded fresh directly from forms.iebc.or.ke in this session (via the governed form_id = constituency_code + 277628 locator, after resetting the portal session from its default by-election context to the 2022 general election via index.php?r=common/set-election&id=5), its sha256 was computed from the downloaded bytes, and the TOTAL row integers were read directly from the rendered page image at 300 DPI. No OCR, machine-candidate pipeline, or prior extraction artifact was used or consulted before recording these values.

same_row_valid_vote_reconciliation.method: Independent visual read of the four presidential candidate total cells on the same final TOTAL row.

row_reconciliation.governed_p23_registered_voters_source: KDA-VOTERS-CON-123-2022 (data/indicators/registry/observations.json), sourced from the pre-election official IEBC First Schedule registered-voters gazette, published 2022-06-21

note: Total Valid Votes, Rejected Ballots and the candidate cells are individually clear and internally reconcile on the printed TOTAL row (candidate sum 26,077 = printed Total Valid Votes). However, the row's own printed Registered Voters figure (42,994) does not exactly match the separately governed P23 registered-voter denominator for this constituency (42,937), a 57-voter gap. Unlike the prison/special-station cases documented elsewhere in this tranche, both pages of this form were reviewed in full and no special-facility polling station (prison, hospital, or similar) was found on either page whose registered-voters count would explain the gap. Left unresolved as a genuine, investigated-but-unexplained denominator gap rather than assumed to be the same pattern without evidence, matching the Ainamoi precedent from an earlier tranche.
